subject: Recap & next steps — private deployment, data residency & air-gap needs
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-17T09:15:00Z
Subject: Recap: private deployment conversation — initial notes and asks

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and the recommended next steps so we all have the same view. Please flag anything I missed or misinterpreted.

High-level drivers you shared
- Regulatory: SHDA (State Health Data Act) requires that patient data reside within US-controlled infrastructure and restricts remote egress for PHI.
- Security posture: air-gapped or highly restricted VPC with no outbound internet egress from the inference hosts; all telemetry must be routed via your on-prem collector.
- Operational: low-latency inference in-region for clinical workflows, but limited maintenance windows and strict change-control.

Primary pain points
1) Network egress restrictions: only a few approved IPs for outbound management; ephemeral ports are heavily constrained.
2) Data residency and auditability: logs/audit trails must be retained on Cedar-managed storage for 7 years and be exportable for audits.
3) Deployment model: preference for Private deployment (VPC or on-prem bundle) with an option for an isolated, air-gapped installation.

Goals we aligned on
- Deliver a proof-of-concept in a Cedar staging VPC within 6–8 weeks to validate latency and integration points.
- Produce a mutual action plan (MAL) with network requirements, maintenance windows, and evidence list for procurement.
- Provide a quantifiable ops runbook for patching and emergency rollback that fits your change-control process.

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA)
- Vanessa: Share the filled "networking_requirements_template.pdf" (attached) and a short checklist for allowed management flows — today EOD.
- Dylan (solutions eng): Validate that our private package can be configured with zero outbound egress and provide required port/protocol list — by 2026-04-20.
- Grace (security): Pull the SOC 2 artifacts we can share and list any gaps related to on-prem installation — by 2026-04-23.
- Emily / IT Procurement: Confirm whether Cedar prefers an on-prem air-gap install or a customer-managed VPC with strict egress controls (one of these will be required to scope infra changes) — by next Tuesday.

Attachments included:
- networking_requirements_template.pdf (fill and return)
- SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx (initial version)

Proposed cadence: 30-min follow-up with your network ops + our solutions engineer next week to walk the template and answer any connectivity questions. I can set something for Wed/Thu — which works best for your team?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@cedarhealth.com>

Cc: IT Procurement <itprocurement@cedarhealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-17T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: private deployment conversation — initial notes and asks

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear summary. That matches our conversation; a couple clarifications from my side:

1) On the deployment model: Cedar's preference is an air-gapped on-prem package if it meets performance SLAs. A VPC option is acceptable only if we can certify no egress and bring all logs back to our SIEM.
2) On audit/artifacts: SHDA auditors will want immutable exportable logs and evidence of KMS control — we need to understand how your Private option integrates with our HSM/KMS or whether Redwood will hand over key material for the enclave.
3) On timelines: the 6–8 week PoC works if we can lock on scope this week. Our network team needs the port/protocol matrix before their maintenance window on 2026-04-26.

I'll coordinate with procurement to confirm the preferred contract vehicle (MSA + SOW) — they should reply with constraints by Monday.

I'll also loop in our network ops lead (cc'd on next thread) for the follow-up deep-dive.

Appreciate it,
Emily Stone
Director, Clinical IT 
Cedar Health
emily.stone@cedarhealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0147

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T10:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Recap: private deployment conversation — network/infra checklist

Vanessa / Grace —

Following Emily's notes, I'm starting the technical assessment. Quick status:
- Our private bundle supports disabling all outbound hosts and running solely via customer-provided ingress proxies. We'll produce a port/protocol matrix; initial estimate is that we need:
  - Management plane: TCP 443 (config only) OR an SFTP window if they prefer file-based updates
  - Model registry sync (one-time): optional, can be via USB transfer for air-gap installs
  - Metrics export: configurable to push to a customer collector, otherwise retained locally and packaged for export

Questions for network ops call:
- Can Cedar provide a jump host for admin operations, or must admin be from inside their private network?
- Are there existing HSM integration patterns we should reuse? (PKCS#11 or existing vendor?)

I'll draft the MAL and the technical appendix today and drop it in the Drive folder. Vanessa — will you schedule the network ops deep-dive for Wed morning? I have availability 09:00–11:30 PT.

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Thanks — I put the MAL & technical appendix (initial draft) in the Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleMAL.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute technical deep-dive with Cedar network ops + our solutions engineering to walk the port/protocol matrix and confirm the admin model. Wed 2026-04-21 09:30 PT or Thu 2026-04-22 10:00 PT — please pick one and I'll send a calendar invite to all.

We will also prepare two deployment options for you to review in the MAL:
- Option A: On-prem air-gapped bundle (full offline install; model artifacts transferred via secure media)
- Option B: Customer-controlled VPC with strict egress rules and customer SIEM ingestion

If procurement confirms they need an MSA + SOW, we'll prepare a narrow SOW scoped to the PoC only to keep procurement cycles short.
